Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

tidygenclust 0.2.0

  • gt_radmix() streams data larger than the memory: its passes read the backing file in chunks, with the next chunk read ahead and alternating directions, and give identical results (options tidygenclust.radmix_stream and tidygenclust.radmix_chunk_mb; a source of genotype likelihoods can give a prefetch function, see inst/include/tidygenclust/radmix_gl_source.h)
  • gt_radmix() is 15-20% faster on genotypes in memory with 8,192 individuals or more: their passes over the individuals now take the loci in chunks too
  • new gl_curvature argument of gt_radmix(): "observed" takes Newton steps with the curvature of the log-likelihood of genotype likelihoods, about 1.5 times faster on low-depth data ("complete", the default, keeps the curvature of the EM algorithm)
  • gt_radmix(init = "svd") computes its SVD with tidypopgen’s gt_pca(): missing genotypes no longer need imputing (also for pseudohaploids), it uses about 1 GB less memory, and it is faster without an optimised BLAS (needs tidypopgen >= 1.1.0)
  • gt_radmix() is 6-24% faster per iteration from K = 7 (more at larger K), with the same results up to rounding
  • gt_radmix() reports in its log the largest change of the estimates at each iteration, and the new step_tol can require it to be small before stopping; a decrease of the log-likelihood no longer counts as convergence
  • gt_radmix(): fix columns that froze when a Newton step met a nearly singular Hessian (e.g. a near-empty cluster at large K); the step is now taken with a small ridge shift
  • gt_radmix() is faster on subsets of individuals that are filtered or reordered (13-27% fewer cycles per pass), with identical results
  • gt_radmix() also fits genotype likelihoods, with the model of NGSadmix (Skotte, Korneliussen & Albrechtsen 2013) and the algorithm of ADMIXTURE. tidygenclust does not store genotype likelihoods: a package that does can provide a method of the new generic gt_radmix_data(), which gives the kernels a C function that reads its likelihoods (see inst/include/tidygenclust/radmix_gl_source.h), so tidygenclust does not depend on it. P then gives the frequency of allele2. Cross-validation (with the deviance of the held-out likelihoods) and starts from the SVD (of the posterior dosages under the emMAF allele frequencies, with svd_power power iterations) are available; use_imputed is not.
  • New gt_adamixture(): ancestry estimation with the python package ADAMIXTURE (Saurina-i-Ricos, Mas Montserrat & Ioannidis 2026), run with reticulate like gt_fastmixture(), on a gen_tibble (including subsets) or on PLINK files. ADAMIXTURE (version 1.8.9, from PyPI, without PyTorch) is installed by default by tgc_tools_install(), or added to an existing environment with the new tgc_adamixture_install(), and its version is reported by tgc_tools_version().
  • New gt_radmix(): ancestry estimation with the ADMIXTURE method (Alexander, Novembre & Lange 2009) and the algorithm of ADMIXTURE (EM priming, block relaxation with constrained Newton steps, and the quasi-Newton acceleration of Zhou, Alexander & Lange 2011), in multithreaded C++ that reads the gen_tibble directly, with the cross-validation of ADMIXTURE (Alexander & Lange 2011) and support for pseudohaploids. Its results are checked against ADMIXTURE and OpenADMIXTURE.jl in the test suite. It stops when the log-likelihood changes by less than a relative 1e-8 (rtol). With init = "svd", runs start from the SVD of the genotypes, as in fastmixture and ADAMIXTURE, for a faster single fit of large datasets. The refits of the folds of cross-validation stop at a relative change of 1e-7 (cv_rtol), which halves the cost of cross-validation on data whose refits are slow to converge, with errors lower by at most 2e-4 in our tests and the same K chosen; cv_max_iter and a larger cv_rtol shorten them further (faster, but with errors biased downwards, more so at larger K), and cv_rtol = rtol refits each fold to convergence. Its computations were sped up by cheaper decoding of the genotypes and likelihood terms and by processing two loci at a time (about 1.3-1.4x), and, on x86-64 Linux, by also compiling them for AVX2 and FMA (about 1.6x in all). A later reorganisation of the computations made fits slightly faster (a few percent), with the same numbers of iterations and estimates that differ from those of earlier development versions only by rounding. Each iteration now reads the genotypes four times instead of five: the log-likelihood of the point an iteration ends at is computed in the same pass as the first update of the next iteration, with the same iterations and estimates. With crossval = TRUE, the fit of each fold computes once which genotypes it hides (a bit mask, one bit per genotype) instead of in every pass, so its passes cost as much as those of the main fit instead of about 1.5 times as much; the cross-validation errors are identical. On x86-64 Linux, the computation of the expected genotypes and of the log-likelihood in each pass is now also compiled for AVX2 and FMA, and the log-likelihood is cheaper; with the fused pass, an iteration takes about 0.8 of the time it took on one core (HGDP, 1043 x 130,943, K = 5), with the same iterations and estimates that differ only by rounding. The work on Q of datasets with fewer than 8,192 individuals is split into more tasks (128 rather than 32), which makes fits on 8 threads 3-6% faster (estimates differ only by rounding). ?gt_radmix describes the algorithm, the reproducibility of the results, and how they compare with those of ADMIXTURE. Supervised analyses, as ADMIXTURE’s --supervised option, are run with the new argument supervised: the population of each reference individual (NA for the individuals to estimate), whose ancestry is then fixed. As in ADMIXTURE, k must equal the number of reference populations, and the columns of Q follow the order of their first appearance (or the levels of a factor); the result lists them in ref_pops. Cross-validation is available, and the fit skips the work of the reference individuals. The estimates are checked against ADMIXTURE in the test suite. Supervised analyses also work with genotype likelihoods.
  • gt_clumppling() is now a native R and C++ port, with modifications, of clumppling 2.0.10 (Liu, Kopelman & Rosenberg 2024, by Xiran Liu).
  • The conda environment is no longer needed by default, as the core functionality is native. tgc_tools_install() gains a tools argument to choose which optional tools to install (fastmixture and ADMIXTURE), and tgc_fastmixture_install() and tgc_admixture_install() add a tool to an existing environment.
  • Fixed the colours of the clusters in the plots of gt_clumppling objects with K >= 10: clusters were ordered as text (“1”, “10”, “2”, …), so the same aligned cluster was drawn in a different colour (and position) for different values of K.
  • The optional tools (fastmixture, ADMIXTURE and ADAMIXTURE) are only available on Linux at the moment: tgc_tools_install() and the other installers explain this on macOS and Windows (on Windows, they said that tidygenclust did not work at all), as the rest of the package does not need conda. On macOS, the OpenMP library of the python tools conflicts with that of R (used by packages such as bigstatsr), which crashes the R session; on Windows, the tools can be used through the WSL.
  • gt_fastmixture() now starts from the SVD-based initialisation of fastmixture by default (random_init = FALSE).
  • gt_fastmixture() now uses the individuals and loci selected in a gen_tibble.
  • gt_fastmixture(threads = ) now limits the number of threads (with the python package threadpoolctl, which tgc_fastmixture_install() now installs): the environment variables used before had no effect once R had started OpenMP, and they stayed set in the R session.
  • subset_gt_clumppling(k = ) selects the right values of K: it failed when k covered all of K_range, selected K = 20 to 29 together with K = 2 (and so on), could not select values of K with gaps (e.g. 17 and 19 in the chicken example), and silently returned an empty object for values of K that were not in K_range.
  • subset_gt_clumppling(indivs = ) checks that the individuals are between 1 and N, rather than silently returning rows of NA.
  • Plots of gt_clumppling objects subset by individuals draw the group boundaries and labels (and the number of runs of each mode) in the right place.
  • The group argument of the plots of gt_clumppling objects can be a factor.
  • autoplot(type = "modes_within_k") checks that k is a single value of K_range: other values gave an empty plot that failed when printed.
  • autoplot(type = "modes") no longer warns for a gt_clumppling object with a single value of K.
  • The vignette and the documentation of autoplot() no longer say that the edges of the ‘modes’ plot are labelled with their cost: they are coloured by it.
  • gt_fastmixture() checks its arguments before starting python, with error messages naming the right arguments, and a single seed (such as the default) can be used with n_runs > 1: it is incremented for each run.
  • On Intel Macs, fastmixture is compiled with the llvm installed by Homebrew (its location was hard-coded for Apple silicon).
  • The safety argument of gt_fastmixture() is deprecated: it was never passed on to fastmixture, which turns on its safety updates by itself when an update is unstable.

tidygenclust 0.1.4

  • Updated clumppling to v2.0.10, which is now installed in the same conda environment as fastmixture (ctidygenclust); the separate cclumppling environment is no longer needed.

tidygenclust 0.1.3

  • Fixed gt_fastmixture() wrapper for fastmixture 1.3.0: P matrices are now returned in the original locus order, and gen_tibble input is shuffled and normalised as in fastmixture, giving the same results as PLINK input.

tidygenclust 0.1.2

  • Updated version of fastmixture to 1.3.0
  • Use pre-tested conda environments to avoid dependency hell.

tidygenclust 0.1.1

  • Updated versions of fastmixture and clumppling

tidygenclust 0.1.0

  • Initial public version
